source.title: AutoInit: Analytic Signal-Preserving Weight Initialization for Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares initialization methods and reports training behavior and accuracy, bearing on initialization, depth, learning rate, and normalization claims. It uses AutoInit and accuracy/stability outcomes rather than directly measuring training classification error as framed in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy, chance-accuracy training failures, signal variance, and whether training succeeds. It does not report training classification error values. Rows use only explicit training or performance outcomes bearing on the tested versions; cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The plain All-CNN-C experiments test activation-dependent signal preservation and whether training succeeds, bearing on V4. Final test accuracy alone does not establish learning speed or trainable depth. The residual-network experiments do not test V3's plain-versus-shortcut comparison or V6's normalization speed comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that analytic architecture-adapted initialization improves performance and training stability across multiple architectures and settings, including normalization-free training, and helps architecture and activation-function search. They do not establish universal superiority or directly demonstrate faster learning and greater trainable depth in plain networks.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces and evaluates AutoInit, an analytic initialization method adapted to each network's layers; it is not a direct reproduction of the claim's cited experiments. It reports accuracy and training stability rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by activation function: CoAtNet improves over baselines with GELU, ReLU and Swish, but not SELU. Results also vary with normalization, learning-rate schedules, dropout, weight decay, and learning rate; AutoInit is reported more robust in several of these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: AutoInit permits training of unnormalized residual networks at depths and learning rates where He initialization fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture-aware initialization can stabilize deep residual networks without batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization changes final accuracy and sensitivity to training hyperparameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture-aware initialization can improve final classification accuracy and robustness to hyperparameter choices.

fits_no_version.finding: The prose reports stable CoAtNet training after normalization removal, but the numerical table column is incomplete.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AutoInit can support normalization-free training of a convolution-attention architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Combining initialization changes with activation centering reduces chance-level failures to 117/200.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation centering together with matched initialization can improve trainability of networks using generated activation functions.

record.problems: The paper's principal training-stability proxy is whether accuracy exceeds chance, not training classification error. Several accuracy comparisons are figure-only in the supplied text; many reported table values are medians of three runs without error bars. The paper does not isolate identity shortcuts against a matched plain-network depth comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying numerical results omitted. Figure 4a contains per-learning-rate accuracy values but was not transcribed separately because the text reports only the learning-rate ranges and stability conclusion; Figure 4b has many schedule-specific curves without prose assigning each numeric value. Figure 1 exact values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and size- or regularization-dependent interpolation.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth-related training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized networks and its prevention by matched identity shortcuts; very deep plain tanh networks and Fixup.

Direct learning-speed comparisons, maximum trainable depth of plain networks, backward-gradient preservation, orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Squared-loss catapult dynamics, initial linearized stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, and edge-of-stability training.
Matched normalization comparisons of accuracy gain over training time and tolerable learning rates; Fixup's speed and stability relative to normalized networks.

missing.what: Empirical forward-signal variance in plain All-CNN-C: default initialization often causes vanishing signals across layers, while AutoInit restores variance to approximately one at weighted layers across activation and dropout settings.

record.verdict_notes: Verdicts use only the supplied text. Residual-network training results and final held-out accuracy are kept distinct from the specific plain-network speed and depth outcomes in V4. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No training classification error results; random or corrupted labels, model-size sweeps, SGD/Adam comparison, and early stopping are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems or spurious-local-minimum frequency results.

Tests ResNet depth, batch normalization removal, and initialization on CIFAR-10; does not compare plain networks with identity shortcuts against otherwise matched plain networks. Does not test the cited special plain tanh initialization or Fixup.

Tests AutoInit against several initialization baselines and varies activation functions and depth. Does not test the specific Glorot, He, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian, or 10,000-layer claims in this version.
No learning-rate-above-stability-limit squared-loss experiments or sharpness measurements.

Tests removal of normalization in residual and transformer settings and reports accuracy/training stability; does not test batch normalization speed or higher-learning-rate tolerance against otherwise matched networks as described in this version.

rows.subject: ResNet-56
rows.operation_detail: Five epochs of training without batch normalization across learning rates, comparing He Normal and AutoInit initializations.
rows.measure: Whether training begins / accuracy after five epochs
rows.baseline: With He Normal, requires a learning rate between 10−8 and 0.5 × 10−3 to begin training.
rows.value: AutoInit stabilizes training; networks remain stable with higher learning rates between 10−4 and 0.05.
rows.locator: Section 6, Stable Initial Learning Rates; Figure 4a
rows.note: Training stability is the paper's stated proxy; training classification error is not reported.
rows.check: Valid initialization-dependent training result, but the network is residual; V4 specifies plain networks. No matched normalization comparison establishes V6, and no plain-network comparison establishes V3.

rows.subject: ResNet-164

rows.measure: Whether training is possible / accuracy after five epochs
rows.baseline: With He Normal, training was not possible because of exploding signals.
rows.value: AutoInit stabilizes training; networks remain stable with higher learning rates between 10−4 and 0.05.
rows.locator: Section 6, Stable Initial Learning Rates; Figure 4a
rows.note: Training stability is the paper's stated proxy; no training-error value is provided.
rows.check: Training rescue in a residual network does not measure V3's shortcut effect or V4's plain-network effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-164
rows.operation_detail: Compared default initialization and AutoInit across warm-up plus cosine-decay learning-rate schedules.

conditions.value: linear warm-up followed by cosine decay to zero; epoch 200 completion

rows.baseline: Comparable performance with AutoInit on the best learning-rate schedules; suboptimal schedules degraded performance more quickly with default initialization.
rows.value: Comparable to or outperforms default initialization across the reported schedules.
rows.note: The paper does not give numeric training-error results.
rows.check: Final accuracy across schedules in a fixed-depth residual network does not measure plain-network learning speed, trainable depth, or depth degradation.

rows.subject: ResNet-164
rows.operation_detail: Compared default initialization and AutoInit with batch normalization removed.
rows.measure: Accuracy / whether training succeeds across learning-rate schedules
rows.baseline: With default initialization, the network fails to train regardless of learning-rate schedule.
rows.value: AutoInit results in high accuracy for the majority of schedules.
rows.note: “Majority” is not quantified in the prose; no training-error values are reported.
rows.check: AutoInit enables normalization-free residual training, but the row does not compare training speed with normalization or test Fixup's recipe. It also lacks V3's plain-versus-residual comparison.

rows.subject: CoAtNet
rows.size_stated: three convolutional blocks with 64 channels, four with 128, six transformer blocks with 256, and three transformer blocks with 512
rows.operation_detail: Compared AutoInit with listed default initialization schemes while removing all normalization layers.
rows.baseline: Glorot Normal 85.73; Glorot Uniform 85.73; He Normal 85.89; He Uniform 85.73; LeCun Normal 85.73; LeCun Uniform 85.73.
rows.uncertainty: Median of three runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The table gives the no-normalization column as a six-row sequence under its initialization labels; the values are assigned in that displayed order.
rows.check: The supplied no-normalization table column is incomplete: the listed six baseline values and AutoInit's 86.80 cannot be recovered from it. The prose establishes stability, not these numerical assignments. Final accuracy does not establish V4 or V6.

rows.subject: All-CNN-C
rows.operation_detail: Compared AutoInit and default initialization with 200 generated activation functions.
rows.measure: Activation functions that did not fail at chance accuracy
rows.baseline: 149 activation functions failed with default initialization.
rows.note: This is training stability summarized by chance-accuracy failures, not training classification error.
rows.check: The training-success proxy improves from 51/200 to 70/200 above chance, but 130/200 still fail. This tests activation-dependent trainability at fixed depth, not learning speed or maximum trainable depth. The dropout adjustment was disabled.

source_check.correct: The reported counts are failures: 130/200 with AutoInit and 149/200 with default initialization. For the row's stated better-than-chance measure, the corresponding counts are 70/200 and 51/200. Accuracy was evaluated on a balanced 5,000-image validation set. State for V4: cannot_determine; this fixed-depth comparison does not measure learning speed or greater trainable depth.
source_check.locator_found: Section 11, Experimental Setup and Stability; Figure 8a.
source_check.problem: The measure and reported_metric name successes, but the values count failures; the partial state also overinterprets fixed-depth validation accuracy as evidence about V4's speed/depth effect.

rows.subject: All-CNN-C
rows.operation_detail: Compared AutoInit++ and default initialization with 200 generated activation functions.
rows.measure: Activation functions that did not fail at chance accuracy
rows.baseline: 149 activation functions failed with default initialization.
rows.note: AutoInit++ also changes the activation functions by subtracting their Gaussian mean, so this is a comparator rather than AutoInit alone.
rows.check: AutoInit++ changes activation functions as well as initialization, so its 117 failures cannot isolate the initialization effect named in V4.

rows.subject: All-CNN-C
rows.operation_detail: Compared AutoInit with Glorot Uniform on the distribution of accuracy across generated activation functions.
rows.measure: Generated activation functions exceeding baseline test accuracy
rows.baseline: 22 of 200 functions with default initialization exceeded 89.10% test accuracy.
rows.value: 26 of 200 with AutoInit exceeded 89.10% test accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: Mann-Whitney U: distribution induced by AutoInit++ exceeds AutoInit, p < 0.05; no uncertainty for this count stated.
rows.note: The count increases by four; the paper's statistical significance comparison is for AutoInit++ versus AutoInit/default.
rows.check: Counts exceeding a performance threshold measure accuracy rather than learning speed or trainable depth. Generated-function evaluations use validation accuracy, although the ReLU threshold is described as test accuracy.
